limitations: Static read only. I did not execute the RED/GREEN tests, compile, ShellCheck or the backfill/reruns20/prior-attempt suites. README GREEN claims are untrusted and unconfirmed.
Only the .py diff was provided. The test script and README are shown as source, not as diff hunks, so I can't confirm they were part of this commit.

I did not see _checkpoint lines 441-479, including how Source.request, source_api and the reconcile `api` wrapper are bound. I can't confirm that the artifact-list response in the artifact-budget test reaches `charge` through a wrapper. I also can't confirm that no other own capacity guard in the file still uses `require`.

In discover mode the added page-1 and overlap fetches (lines 495 and 497) are called directly on `source_api.request`. They are not passed through `charge` and not counted in `calls`, unlike the primary page at line 490. The overlap fetch already behaved this way. The total is at most 3 pages, each bounded by the `len <= page_size` check. I did not treat it as a defect, but those extra responses are not subject to the 2MiB/32MiB guards.

The new head-deep test asserts page 1 is fetched, at most 3 pages are fetched, and the selectors are unique. It does not assert that the distinct overlap page is still fetched or that the overlap schedule is unchanged. I confirmed overlap preservation only by reading the code.

The artifact-budget test covers only the 2MiB per-response path. Typed propagation for the 4096-call and 32MiB aggregate guards inside the receipt-artifact handler is not tested. It follows from the same class and the same `except DiscoveryBudgetError: raise`.

`State.request` wraps any exception after an uncertain write, including a DiscoveryBudgetError from `charge`, into a plain ValueError('discovery write uncertain...'). That path is outside the assess handler and I did not treat it as part of this repair.

Other `except ValueError` branches in assess (lines 168-171, 181-186) and the prior-attempt lookup (lines 548-550) let the budget error escape only because its fixed messages don't match `_source_fetch_unavailable` or the 'not approved'/'source changed'/'revoked' tokens. This is not a type-based rethrow. It is correct for the current messages.

Lower-layer archive/transport ValueError taxonomy is unchanged and outside this repair. I did not verify that `archive.receipts.receipt_artifact` or `archive.append_delivery` preserve a DiscoveryBudgetError raised beneath them. I make no claim that lower-layer capacity or identity errors are hardened.
Native and cadence acceptance are not proved by this review.
structured_output.review_summary:
By inspection, both residuals are repaired and nothing introduced needs changes. I did not run any tests, and the limitations list the places where I couldn't verify behavior.

**Newhead:** the old schedule polled the overlap page only. Now every discover call with page>1 also fetches page 1 directly. The distinct overlap page is fetched only when it is neither 1 nor the primary page, so there are at most 3 unique fetches. The overlap_page and overlap_until advance logic is unchanged. `primary_short` still reads only the primary page, so the short or empty wrap is preserved. Dedupe and the immutable-identity check run across the merged pages. The checkpoint still reports `coverage_complete` false, so no historical coverage is claimed.

**Budget propagation:** `DiscoveryBudgetError` subclasses ValueError. It is raised at the three own guards: per-response, aggregate and call count, the last in both `State.request` and `source_read`. The conditions are logically identical to the old `require` forms. The 4096, 2097152 and 33554432 thresholds and the messages are unchanged. In `assess`, `except DiscoveryBudgetError: raise` sits before the broad `except ValueError`. It comes after `(RuntimeError, OSError)`, which the typed error is not part of. A budget error in the receipt-artifact try therefore no longer becomes `proof-unavailable`. The other ValueError branches also let it escape, because its messages don't match any soft token. The artifact-budget test now requires the typed failure, an unchanged ref and no outcomes. That matches the intended RED-to-hard-failure change.

**Remaining gaps:** I found no defect to flag. The limitations cover the unseen lines, the uncharged extra page fetches, the test coverage gaps and the lower-layer taxonomy. I did not assert that the lower layers are hardened or that native or cadence behavior is proved.
